text:
alice_support: Heads-up — Acme reported a 401 invalid_api_key on /v1/chat after they copied the key from the dashboard. They say the key looks correct in the UI but API rejects it.
jamie_sre: thanks, can you paste the exact Authorization header they used (redact the secret) so we can repro quickly?
alice_support: pasted from customer (redacted):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat \
  -H \"Authorization: ApiKey org_01AB23/abcd-efgh-ijkl\" \
  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-1","input":"hi"}'
```
jamie_sre: ah — that slash looks suspicious. our hosted keys are of the form `rk_live_...` or `sk_...` (no path segment). Do they have an org-scoped copy button in the UI?
alice_support: they said they clicked the copy button on the org keys page and shared screenshot; the copy string included `org_<orgid>/` before the key.
jamie_sre: filing quick hypothesis: the UI adds an `org_<id>/` prefix when showing org-level key identifiers (to make them human-distinct) but the copy button accidentally included the prefix in the clipboard. our header validation rejects `/` characters in the token and returns 401 with code invalid_api_key.
jamie_sre: quick check — run this (locally redacted) and see if it succeeds:
```
# same curl but with the leading org_<id>/ removed from the token
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat \
  -H \"Authorization: ApiKey abcd-efgh-ijkl\" \
  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-1","input":"hi"}'
```
alice_support: customer tried that and it worked immediately, confirmed. :tada:
jamie_sre: good — root cause confirmed. I'll open an SRE ticket to update header validation logging to include a clearer error message for slashes in tokens, and a product bug to stop the copy button from including the org prefix.
jamie_sre: created SRE-2543 (better invalid key logging) and UI-1187 (copy button include prefix).
deploy-bot: deployment 2023.11.08.18:32 rolled to staging (ui-copy-fix branch) :white_check_mark:
alice_support: customer is unblocked and emailed the workaround. marking this thread as resolved but leaving notes for follow-up. :thumbsup:
jamie_sre: postmortem note: add client-side sanity check in SDKs to reject tokens with path separators and include a helpful error pointing to the docs (auth tokens should not contain '/').
alice_support: ack, will add to the support KB entry: "401 invalid_api_key — check for accidental org/ prefix when copying key from org page."
